instructions: Cut the calamari tubes into rings about 1/2 inch thick. If the tentacles are large, cut them in half. Spread everything on paper towels and pat it very dry.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, semolina, salt, pepper, paprika and oregano.

Pour the vegetable oil into a heavy pot so it's about 2 inches deep. Heat it over medium-high until it reaches 350°F, about 6 minutes. If you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Drop in a pinch of the flour mix. It should sizzle right away and float.
Meanwhile, cut the lemons into wedges.
Working in 3 batches, toss one third of the calamari in the flour mix until each ring is coated. Lift the pieces into a sieve and shake off the extra flour.
Lower that batch into the hot oil a few pieces at a time. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until pale gold. Stand back a little. They'll spatter. The longer they fry, the chewier they get.
Transfer the batch to a plate lined with paper towels, and sprinkle with a pinch of salt. Coat and fry the other 2 batches the same way, coating each right before it goes in the oil.
Taste a ring. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve right away with the lemon wedges.
method_notes: My Greek Dish (the lead, 4.78 from 591) dusts cleaned calamari rings in bread flour and semolina seasoned with salt, pepper, paprika and oregano, with no batter, and fries them for 2 to 3 minutes. Other Greek versions agree on the thin flour coating and a short fry, since longer frying makes the squid rubbery. Flour amounts follow the lead, and the oil temperature (350°F) is added as a target with a flour-pinch check. Served with lemon only, as in the lead, so it stays dairy-free (tzatziki is the usual extra). Total about 22 minutes.
